problem:
Consider the solid enclosed between the parabolic cylinders $y=4{x}^{2}$ and $y=1-2{z}^{2},$ whose volume can be written in terms of double integrals, as follows:

$$
V={\int }_{-1/2}^{1/2}{\int }_{a(x)}^{b(x)}\,f(x,z)\,dz\,dx
$$

What is ${a}^{2}+{b}^{2}+f?$

activity_context.topic_title: Calculating Volumes of Solids Using Triple Integrals

feedback.problem:
Consider the solid enclosed between the paraboloids $z=-3+6{x}^{2}+5{y}^{2}$ and $z=-1+5{x}^{2}+3{y}^{2},$ whose volume can be written in terms of double integrals, as follows:

$$
V={\int }_{-\sqrt{2}}^{\sqrt{2}}{\int }_{a(x)}^{b(x)}\,f(x,y)\,dy\,dx
$$

What is ${a}^{2}+{b}^{2}+f?$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we need to determine the projection of the intersection of our surfaces onto the $xy$-plane. So, let's find where they intersect.

$$
\begin{aligned}-3+6{x}^{2}+5{y}^{2} & =-1+5{x}^{2}+3{y}^{2} \\ {x}^{2}+2{y}^{2} & =2\end{aligned}
$$

So, the projection of the intersection in the $xy$-plane is an ellipse.

Notice that our solid can be written as a type I region: 

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,y)\in D,\,\,-3+6{x}^{2}+5{y}^{2}\le z\le -1+5{x}^{2}+3{y}^{2}},
$$

where $D$ is the interior of the ellipse ${x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}=2.$ 

As a result, the volume of $R$ is given by 

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={∭}_{R}\text{d}V \\  & ={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{-3+6{x}^{2}+5{y}^{2}}^{-1+5{x}^{2}+3{y}^{2}}\text{d}z]\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-1+5{x}^{2}+3{y}^{2})-(-3+6{x}^{2}+5{y}^{2})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}2-{x}^{2}-2{y}^{2}\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, notice that the boundary of $D$ consists of

- the lower part $y=-\sqrt{1-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}},$ and

- the upper part $y=\sqrt{1-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}},$

for $-\sqrt{2}\le x\le \sqrt{2}.$ 

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}2-{x}^{2}-2{y}^{2}\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{-\sqrt{2}}^{\sqrt{2}}{\int }_{-\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}/2}}^{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}/2}}\,2-{x}^{2}-2{y}^{2}\,dy\,dx.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}^{2}+{b}^{2}+f & ={(-\sqrt{1-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}})}^{2}+{(\sqrt{1-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}})}^{2}+(2-{x}^{2}-2{y}^{2}) \\  & =1-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+1-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+(2-{x}^{2}-2{y}^{2}) \\  & =4-2{x}^{2}-2{y}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
